candidates.exact_span: in order for a permittee to be in compliance with the Forum's municipal discharges criteria, the incremental increase in salinity shall be 400 mg/L or less, which is considered to be a reasonable incremental increase above the flow weighted average salinity of the intake water supply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the baseline Forum municipal salinity incremental-increase limit (400 mg/L above flow-weighted average intake salinity) against which reported measurements may be compared; different readings of 'incremental increase,' 'salinity,' or the intake flow-weighted average basis would change the applicable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: However, the permitting authority may permit a discharge in excess of the 400 mg/L incremental increase at the time of issuance or reissuance of a NPDES discharge permit, upon satisfactory demonstration by the permittee that it is not practicable to attain the 400 mg/L limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides an exception pathway allowing a higher enforceable limit than 400 mg/L if practicability is demonstrated; whether this exception applies at issuance/reissuance changes which numeric limit governs compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: April 10, 2015, the facility demonstrated that it was economically impractical to attain the net 400 mg/L incremental increase limit at that time. Because of that demonstration, EPA allowed a temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L for the previous permit cycle, provided that the facility will diligently control and reduce TDS in their discharge (i.e., maintaining the formulated BMP activities, monitoring its effluent quality and quantity on a regular basis, and completing $14 million upgrades at the WWTP to improve overall effluent quality (i.e., reducing TDS in their discharges)).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies a prior-cycle temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L tied to a 2015 impracticability demonstration and conditional BMP, monitoring, and upgrade obligations; interpretation of whether this limit or its conditions carry forward, and what 'net incremental increase' and '30-day average' mean, would change applicable limit comparisons (A) and whether ongoing effluent quality/quantity monitoring was required (B).

candidates.exact_span: The City of Farmington has constructed a new sampling station where water intake samplings have been conducted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Describes intake sampling location and practice used to support limit derivation; different interpretation of where/when intake samples must be taken affects monitoring-obligation applicability (B) and whether intake-based calculations or missing-intake-data cases are adequately documented (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA believes the TDS data collected during the past permit cycle are sufficient and representative of facility existing operation conditions and can be used to derive the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that past-cycle TDS data will be used to derive the final 30-day average net incremental increase limit; whether data are 'sufficient and representative' affects the derived enforceable limit value (A), implied monitoring/data-collection expectations (B), and how periods without adequate TDS or intake data should be classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA cannot grant the permittee request of keeping the temporary 30-day average TDS net incremental increase limit of 497 mg/L in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicitly rejects continuation of the 497 mg/L temporary limit in the draft permit, implying a different final limit applies; misreading this would cause incorrect limit selection for compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: To protect and maintain existing water quality as required by 40 CFR §122(4)(d) and to prevent further degradation of water quality in the San Juan River in accordance with 40 CFR §131.12, Subsection A of 20.6.4.8 NMAC, the New Mexico Continuing Planning Process –
candidates.computation_change_reason: Invokes antidegradation and continuing-planning regulatory bases for setting the final limit; interpretation of how these provisions constrain the derived 30-day average net incremental increase limit could change the enforceable numeric limit applied in the draft permit even though the segment cuts off before stating the final value.
